newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IFC to boost investments in Romania.
newsitem.headline: IFC to boost investments in Romania.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) plans to expand its investments in Romania provided the country pursues its economic reforms, the IFC's top European official said on Friday.
"The investments depend on the nature and pace of continued economic reforms," Harold Rosen, IFC director for Europe, told a news conference.
The Fund's investment plans include the local capital market, a leasing company and a commercial bank as well as participation in communication and energy sector privatisations.

The IFC is a member of the World Bank Group and the largest multilateral source of equity and loan financing for private-sector projects in developing countries. Romania has been a member of the IFC since 1990.
Rosen praised the reform steps Romania had made since last year when centrists replaced the former leftist government.
"We have put in about $200 million of financing, the vast majority since the present government came to power."

That figure included the financing of two recently-launched GSM mobile telephone companies and investment in the Alcatel Network System Romania, a telecommunications joint venture company with France's Alcatel.

In recent months Romania's government has reduced inflation, liberalised markets and introduced market-oriented legislation to attract foreign investors previously slow to put their money into the Balkan country.
